title: Animal Care Skills I
description: Practical application of animal care skills and principles of animal care and management. Opportunity to participate in the health care team involved in the care, management, and husbandry of program animals. Students will work in teams to provide appropriate nursing care for all program animals. Emphasis on the basic principles and application of clinical facility management, care of resident teaching animals, and routine maintenance duties. Includes dog and cat behavior, low stress handling, medical records, professionalism, and euthanasia. Intended for students in the Veterinary Technology Program; enrollment is limited to students accepted in the program.
outcomes: Conscientiously and safely perform assigned routine husbandry duties for veterinary technology teaching animals.
Discuss the human animal bond, medical records including SOAP (subjective, objective, assessment and plan) technique and behavior assessments.
objectives: Demonstrate standard operating procedures for animal care, approved by the Foothill College Veterinary Technology Program IACUC.
Demonstrate standard operating procedures for veterinary technology laboratory and facilities care.
Demonstrate professionalism in providing for the needs of program animals.
Describe basic principles of dog and cat behavior.
Discuss low stress handling techniques for dogs and cats.
Demonstrate the principles of Problem Oriented Veterinary Medical Record keeping to writing records and reading case studies at Foothill College.
Discuss the role of the technician in humane euthanasia.
content: Orientation to lab, animal care facility
Routine animal care and husbandry requirements
Care and safe use of cleaning equipment
Daily veterinary care of the teaching animal colony
Animal care according to standard practices
Medical communication with peers and supervisors
Review of the PLEASE CARE model for patient care
Working with other veterinary technology students
Basic principles of dog and cat behavior
Role of veterinary technician in animal behavior
Canine behavior at different stages of development
Common behavior problems in the dog
Feline behavior at different stages of development
Low stress handling techniques for dogs and cats
Handling techniques in the veterinary clinic
History taking in small animal medicine
